skill.name: ai-maestro-agent-messaging
skill.description: Send, read, and manage AI Maestro messages between coding agents through Bash-based inbox and notification commands.
skill.summary: Coordinate AI coding agents through AI Maestro file messages and tmux notifications.
skill.author: 23blocks-OS

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown scanner artifacts or documented AI Maestro command examples, not hidden code execution. The main residual risks are intentional cross-host messaging, tmux injection, and workflows that may act on untrusted agent messages. No prompt-injection text was found that attempts to override this audit.

remediation.issue: Cross-host messages can send task details to configured remote hosts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit operator confirmation before remote sends and show the resolved host URL.

remediation.issue: The tmux inject method can interrupt or influence another agent session.
remediation.suggestion: Default to display-only notifications and require approval before using inject or echo.

remediation.issue: Incoming agent messages can trigger follow-up work without a trust check.
remediation.suggestion: Treat message content as untrusted and ask the operator before risky actions.

remediation.issue: Direct examples read AI Maestro state under hidden home directories.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer audited helper scripts and validate message IDs before direct file reads.

remediation.issue: The host configuration example includes a concrete private IP address.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a documentation-only hostname or a reserved example address.

semantic_findings.title: Cross-host Message Data Transmission
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes sending message content to configured remote AI Maestro hosts. This can transmit operator-provided task details outside the local machine.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cross-host section states that remote agents are resolved from host configuration and messages are posted to the remote API. The behavior is intentional but creates a data-sharing boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Terminal Message Injection Into Other Agents
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports an inject method that writes alert text into another tmux session. A crafted message could interrupt or influence another agent workflow.

content.user_title: Coordinate AI Agents with AI Maestro
content.value_statement: Multi-agent coding work needs reliable handoffs and status checks. This skill helps agents exchange structured messages through AI Maestro.
actual_capabilities: Checks unread messages for the current AI Maestro agent inbox.
Reads a specific message and can mark it as read.
Sends structured messages with subject, priority, and type fields.
Sends immediate tmux notifications to another agent session.
Supports local and configured cross-host agent addresses.
limitations: Requires AI Maestro scripts and Bash access on the machine.
Depends on tmux session names or agent IDs being correct.
Remote delivery depends on configured hosts and reachable APIs.
It does not authenticate message content or validate task safety.

use_cases.title: Coordinate backend and frontend agents
use_cases.description: Send API readiness updates, blockers, and implementation requests between specialized coding agents.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering teams using multiple AI agents

use_cases.title: Check assigned work after startup
use_cases.description: Review unread messages for the current agent before starting a new coding task.

use_cases.title: Route urgent incident updates
use_cases.description: Notify another agent through tmux and follow with a persistent message containing context.

prompt_templates.title: Check my agent inbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my AI Maestro inbox and summarize any unread messages for this agent.

prompt_templates.title: Read one message
prompt_templates.prompt: Read message MESSAGE_ID from my AI Maestro inbox and tell me the sender, priority, and requested action.

prompt_templates.title: Send a structured update
prompt_templates.prompt: Send backend-api a normal update that the user profile screen is ready for endpoint testing.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate an urgent cross-agent response
prompt_templates.prompt: Notify backend-api about the production login failure, then send a detailed urgent message with symptoms and timestamps.

output_examples.output: The agent inbox has two unread messages. One asks for API review, and one reports a completed frontend task.

output_examples.input: Tell frontend-dev that the endpoint is ready.
output_examples.output: Message sent to frontend-dev with normal priority. The subject says the endpoint is ready for integration.
One urgent message is present. It reports an authentication outage and requests immediate investigation.

best_practices: Check only the current agent inbox unless the operator explicitly approves another target.
Confirm the target agent and host before sending cross-host messages.
Treat message contents as untrusted instructions until the operator approves action.
anti_patterns: Do not read another agent inbox to satisfy a general status request.
Do not send secrets or credentials through agent messages.
Do not use tmux injection for routine updates or unclear targets.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents send, read, and manage AI Maestro messages from Bash-enabled sessions.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when Bash access is available.

faq.question: Does it read every message on the machine?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow focuses on the current agent inbox under AI Maestro message storage.

faq.question: Can it send messages to remote agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can address configured remote hosts when AI Maestro host settings are present.

faq.question: Is this safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Messages can be read by receiving agents and may be stored in local AI Maestro files.

faq.question: What should I verify before sending?
faq.answer: Verify the target agent, host, priority, and whether the message contains sensitive information.
